shortName: Alice L. Walton School of Medicine
additionalCoursework: AWSOM does not have any required prerequisite courses. Instead, applicants are expected to demonstrate a strong foundation in the humanities, math, and sciences by completing a minimum of 24 credit hours with breadth and depth in the math and sciences in an undergraduate, graduate, or post-baccalaureate educational program.

medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Students have a variety of opportunities to engage in leadership, community service, and career development. Student Council represents the student body, shaping processes and traditions while fostering collaboration with faculty and administration. Medical students serve on standing committees, providing valuable input and leadership experience. 'Houses', led by peer representatives, cultivate collaboration and wellness. Students can develop new or join Student Interest Groups (SIGs) focused on specialties, arts, athletics, and more, along with chapters of national organizations that expand opportunities for advocacy and professional growth opportunities.
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
Our 154,000 sq ft. state-of-the-art School of Medicine facility is designed to foster innovation, collaboration, wellness, and excellence in medical education. Equipped with advanced technology, including simulation labs and interactive learning environments, our facility provides students with hands-on, real-world experience. 

Located in one of the fastest-growing communities in the country, Northwest Arkansas offers endless opportunities for students to explore their interests. Whether it's music, art, sports, recreation, food, or theatre, there are ample opportunities to explore your interests independently or with friends and family.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Medical students have ample rental options near campus, including reserved AWSOM student apartments at local apartments. Opening in 2027, dedicated housing will ensure students have easy access to trails and offerings at Crystal Bridges, campus, and nearby downtown Bentonville.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Our Whole Health emphasizes well-being for all students. Support systems include access to peer tutoring, mental health resources that address specific needs for medical students. and students are encouraged to establish or join interest groups to build community and advocate for equity in medicine. 'Houses' foster a safe space for collaboration, mentorship, and peer support, while institutional policies protect against discrimination and ensure equitable treatment.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: AWSOM’s wellness programs promote well-being through physical, mental, emotional, and financial health support. Rooted in our mission, AWSOM offers comprehensive mental health services in partnership with a local counseling center, including therapy, access to psychiatric nurse practitioners, and onsite psychologists. For physical wellness, students receive prioritized health care at local primary care clinics, have access to the campus fitness center, and can participate in organized classes like yoga and guided meditation. Wellness workshops throughout the year cover topics like nutrition, resilience, and self-care, leveraging local trails and community resources. Financial wellness support includes budgeting workshops, personalized loan counseling, and resources to reduce financial stress. Wellness coaches are available to students who will assist them in achieving their health and well-being goals, as well as offer strategies for physical, mental, and emotional balance.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Casual, proper fit, clean, and modest clothing is acceptable in non-clinical environments. Business-professional attire with a clean white coat and ID badge is required for clinical encounters.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Faculty have an open-door policy and encourage students to connect with them regularly. Learning specialists, career/ academic advisors, and student life officers are available via student affairs.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students will have Standardized Patient (SPs) interactions starting the 1st month & supervised interactions with clinical patients within the Early Clinical Experience course midway through Phase 1.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: The ARCHES curriculum is delivered in an active learning and integrated format.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinic exposure begins early in year 1 in primary care clinics through the Early Clinical Experience course. Core clerkships in year 3, which adds inpatient, surgery, and ambulatory experiences.
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: Students are placed in quartiles for the Medical Student Performance Evaluation.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: There are both mandatory and non-mandatory instructional formats. All active learning sessions will require attendance.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
The Alice L. Walton School of Medicine (AWSOM) offers a transdisciplinary, longitudinal MD curriculum integrating six themes—Art of Healing, Research, Clinical, Health Systems Science, Embracing Whole Health, and Science of Medicine (ARCHES)—across four phases. Phase 1 emphasizes foundational sciences, clinical skills, and the Integrated Principles of Medicine course (IPM) that continues through Phases 2–4. In Phase 2, organ-system-based courses build on clinical and research training. Phase 3 focuses on core clerkships across diverse medical settings, while Phase 4 offers electives and a residency-prep course. Learning is enhanced by a flipped classroom model, small groups, simulation, and other active learning methods.
The ARCHES curriculum enhances medical education with a whole-person approach to care that takes inclusive and collaborative approaches to care designed to promote resilience, prevent disease, and restore health.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: AWSOM students are encouraged to explore their career interests in all specialties, including primary care. Through early clinical experiences in Phase 1 and 2, students will be exposed to family and internal medicine settings. Phase 3 focuses on core clerkships across diverse medical settings. Phase 4 offers students opportunities to explore various specialties and prepare for residency. AWSOM's curriculum trains students to succeed in any medical specialty they pursue.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Students learn the basic principles of research and evidence-based medical practice, including how to effectively locate, analyze, synthesize, and apply medical literature. In the process, they are supported in developing the skills and practices needed to become life-long learners by fostering curiosity and inquiry. Students will design, implement, evaluate, and present a unique scholarly project. Scholarly endeavors will require students to define an area of need, reflect on how to meet that need, research the literature and existing resources, implement a potential solution, evaluate their project, and disseminate their findings. Students have access to mentors from various research and clinical venues to support them in this activity.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Students will engage in service learning and have various opportunities to serve the local Northwest Arkansas and regional communities.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Students are required to complete a scholarly project for graduation as part of our longitudinal research course.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: AWSOM has extensive affiliation agreements with Northwest Arkansas regional hospitals and clinics.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem:
Phase 1 & 2 years: Pass, Pass with Remediation, Fail 
Phase 3 & 4 years: Honors, High Pass, Pass, Pass with Remediation, Fail

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
Founded in 2021, Alice L. Walton School of Medicine (AWSOM) is a nonprofit, four-year MD program that will enhance traditional medical education with the arts, humanities, and Whole Health principles. The School’s culture embraces self-care to empower students to care for their own well-being as well as that of their patients. 

The state-of-the-art medical education facility is located in Bentonville, Arkansas. Is designed to foster a culture of student well-being to empower future physicians to care for their patients as well as themselves.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Mission
Alice L. Walton School of Medicine trains physicians who are devoted to transforming the health of medically underserved and rural communities in Arkansas, its surrounding states, and beyond. AWSOM physicians make a difference by pioneering whole health principles, deploying contemporary technologies, and developing novel partnerships to bridge the gaps to high quality medical care and to promote health and well-being for all individuals and communities.

Vision
Equip and support physicians and health professionals to successfully tackle the healthcare challenges of the 21st century.

Values
-Empathy
-Self-Care
-Humanism
-Entrepreneurialism
-Community Focus

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Per AAMC Application and Acceptance Protocols, admitted students are given two weeks to respond to an offer of admission. Response time is reduced as we approach the academic start date.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: Applicants must submit between three and five letters of recommendation. If their premedical advising office provides a committee letter that compiles feedback from multiple letter writers, it will meet our requirements. All letters must be signed or on official letterhead and submitted through the AMCAS Letters of Evaluation/Recommendation service.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: We strongly recommend applicants choose letter writers who know them well and can attest to their desire and qualifications for pursuing a career in medicine. Letters from family members and/or friends are discouraged.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay:
The goal of the interview day at AWSOM is not only for us to get to know you, but also for you to get to know us and start picturing yourself as an AWSOM medical student. Interview day is organized to give select applicants a detailed introduction to the many exciting opportunities AWSOM offers medical students. By the end of the interview day, through engaging conversations with faculty and staff, you will understand what it will be like to be a medical student at AWSOM.

Interviews are offered to select applicants by invitation. Additional information and instructions on selecting an interview day are sent via email.
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: Invitations will be sent beginning late July/ early August. Interviews will begin in late August 2026 and continue until February 2027.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Interviews are two 30 minute one-on-one  interviews. Interviewers are blinded to MCAT performance, academic background, and biographic information. The rest of the interview day is designed for applicants to learn about AWSOM and ask questions.
medSchoolApplication.regionalInterview: N/A. All interviews will be conducted via Zoom.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: All interviews will be conducted via Zoom.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: Applicants who meet our minimum requirements
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: AWSOM is a private medical school with no required relationship. Applicants must be a US Citizen or US Permanent Resident to be eligible for admission.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: For more information, see our website www.alwmedschool.org/admissions/
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
AWSOM’s admissions philosophy emphasizes our mission and values aligned approach to identifying applicants who mostly strongly align with our mission, vision, and learning community. Applicants who meet our minimum requirements will be provided instructions on completing a supplemental application. Once the supplemental application, application fee, and required letters of recommendation are received, completed files are reviewed for an interview decision. All interviews will be conducted virtually and held on Friday afternoons. 

Applicants can expect email communication at each point in the application process and information published in the admissions portal. All applicants are expected to comply fully and professionally with AAMC Admissions Protocols. Admitted students are required to select “Plan to Enroll” and “Commit to Enroll” through AMCAS by assigned deadlines.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: A strong foundation in math and sciences is critical to success in medical school. This is typically demonstrated by completing upper-level science courses. Course and MCAT performance are considered in our review process. All lifetime scores, scoring trends, as well as section scores will be included in our evaluation process.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: A minimum total score of 500 is required.

medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: We understand the diverse pathways applicants may pursue on their journey towards a career in medicine. While we accept coursework taken at a community college, we encourage applicants to complete advanced science courses at a regionally accredited four-year institution.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Information about how to upload these documents to the admissions portal will be provided to applicants electronically.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
TUITION FREE FOR FIRST FIVE COHORTS
AWSOM will waive all tuition and most fees for the first five cohorts of students for all four years of medical school. 
Additionally, AWSOM has developed a comprehensive financial wellness program that begins upon acceptance and continues through graduation. The program is designed to provide our students with valuable resources, foster connections with financial experts, and offer sessions to build essential financial literacy skills that will benefit them beyond medical school. The program also includes personalized budgeting and financial wellness check-ins.

medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
AWSOM utilizes a comprehensive approach in evaluating experiences, personal attributes, and academic preparation in selecting applicants who most strongly align with our mission, values, and learning community. Successful applicants will have:

-A strong commitment to serving others and the community
-Meaningful exposure to and understanding of the medical profession
-Team and leadership skills
-Demonstrated ability to perform well in an academic setting
-Commitment to Whole Health and self-care
-Evidence of intellectual curiosity, creativity, innovation, and a dedication to lifelong learning
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Applicants are strongly encouraged to engage in meaningful medical activities, including volunteering, clinical work, shadowing, etc., that reflect their commitment to the medical profession.
